title: Northloop Payments Risk Note: Sales Surge Reserve on On-Demand Payouts
content:
Because an on-demand payout is sent ahead of the payout schedule, Northloop keeps back an account-level reserve from a Northloop Payments on-demand payout when the seller's sales are surging.

**Rule.** The account-level reserve is the reserve base sales times the reserve rate times one minus the fulfillment relief, rounded to the cent. The reserve rate is 0.15 when the seller's current performance standing level is Below Standard Level, Developing Seller Level, Standard Level or Above Standard Level and the sales surge ratio is at least 1.5; it is 0.05 when the level is Top Rated Level or Preferred Partner Level and the sales surge ratio is at least 1.5; otherwise it is 0. The sales surge ratio is twelve times the sale credits of the last month divided by the sale credits of the last twelve months, and it is 0 when no sale credit was booked in the last twelve months.

It is deducted from the on-demand payable amount together with any other holdback kept back from the payout; the on-demand payout so obtained is never below zero, is capped at the plan's maximum per payout and is rounded to the cent. What is kept back stays in the balance and is paid with later scheduled payouts.

A window of the last month or twelve months takes in the ledger entries dated after the same calendar day one or twelve months before the request date, up to and including the request date. The level is the seller's current level on the Seller Performance Standing record.

## Reserve rate

| Current Seller Performance Standing level | Sales surge ratio | Reserve rate |
|---|---|---|
| Below Standard Level, Developing Seller Level, Standard Level or Above Standard Level | at least 1.5 | 0.15 |
| Top Rated Level or Preferred Partner Level | at least 1.5 | 0.05 |
| any level | below 1.5 | 0 |

## Hypothetical worked example

Sale credits of the last month 20000.00 USD, of the last twelve months 120000.00 USD: the sales surge ratio is twelve times 20000.00, that is 240000.00, divided by 120000.00, giving 2.0, at least 1.5. At Standard Level the reserve rate is 0.15. With reserve base sales of 20000.00 USD and a fulfillment relief of 0.25, the account-level reserve is 20000.00 times 0.15 times 0.75, that is 2250.00 USD. With last-month sale credits of 14000.00 USD the ratio would be 1.4 and the reserve rate 0.
